crosswalks.label: Web and Digital Interface Designers
crosswalks.rationale: The occupation includes usability, human-computer interaction and user/interface evaluation but combines research with design/implementation responsibilities that the AXM UX Researcher intentionally does not own.

crosswalks.label: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
crosswalks.rationale: The occupation includes surveys/questionnaires, opinions/preferences, satisfaction research, reporting and collaboration with statisticians, but its market-demand, pricing, campaign and commercial-analysis goals are outside UX Research ownership.

crosswalks.label: Ergonomics of human-system interaction — Human-centred design for interactive systems
crosswalks.rationale: Public metadata confirms a human-centred-design reference relevant to user/context research; under the source policy its copyrighted standard text remains reference-only and is not ingested.

findings.summary: No single O*NET occupation cleanly equals UX Researcher: one adjacent occupation blends design/HCI/usability work, while another contributes survey/opinion research but is oriented toward market analysis.
findings.rationale: The current body already separates research evidence from Product and Design authority; a many-to-one/partial crosswalk preserves that professional boundary better than forcing one external occupation code.

findings.summary: Adjacent occupational evidence adds survey, questionnaire, poll and structured-interview data collection as recurring research methods alongside qualitative observation/usability work.
method_labels: O*NET occupation task evidence from adjacent research occupation
findings.rationale: The existing body emphasizes interviews, contextual inquiry, usability and sampling, but quantitative/survey instrument design and its statistical boundary are not first-class machinery.

findings.summary: Research-oriented occupational evidence includes preparing reports and collaborating with statisticians or other specialists to analyze findings, reinforcing research communication and specialist handoffs as normal work.
method_labels: O*NET occupation task evidence from adjacent research occupation
findings.rationale: The body emits findings packets but could reconstruct audience-specific reporting/visualization and a stronger Statistician/Methodologist consultation path for quantitative studies.

findings.summary: Market Research occupational evidence also includes market forecasting, pricing, campaigns and commercial demand analysis that should not be imported merely because survey/research methods overlap.
findings.rationale: Importing the whole adjacent occupation would turn UX Research into marketing/business analysis and violate the package's product/research boundaries.

gaps_against_body.description: Research quantitative/survey instrument design, sampling and analysis ownership deeply enough to define what UX Research can execute itself versus when it hands methodology or inference to Research Methodologist/Statistician.
Add explicit research reporting/visualization and stakeholder-communication machinery that preserves evidence traceability and does not convert findings into product decisions.

contradictions.description: The AXM UX Researcher boundary spans research structures found across adjacent O*NET occupations while intentionally excluding their design/implementation and marketing responsibilities; no exact one-code mapping is established.

nonclaims: This packet does not declare either O*NET occupation equivalent to UX Researcher.
Market forecasting, pricing, advertising/campaign analysis and product-design authority are not imported from adjacent occupations.
ISO 9241-210 standard text is not ingested or reproduced; only public metadata/reference status is used under the research source policy.
This research does not substitute synthetic/model personas for participant evidence.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: No participant consent, privacy, product-decision, statistical-inference or legal authority is created by this research packet.
